title: CRIC GLOF Ontology Specification
summary: Defines the Glacial Lake Outburst Flood domain ontology: type hierarchy, event fields, trigger and failure-mechanism vocabularies, susceptibility indicators, training labels and model task separation.
notes: SPEC vs PRD ambiguity resolved to SPEC. Dominant content is a data/ontology contract: type hierarchies, required/recommended entity fields, and closed controlled vocabularies (failure mechanisms, stability states, training labels) the system must honor. Competing PRD signals: file lives under docs/CRIC-PRD-v0.1/ (PRD-family path) and the final section is 'v0.1 Acceptance Criteria' with nine criteria. Per ambiguity rule, higher-precedence signal (SPEC > PRD) wins; the acceptance-criteria section is one section of nineteen. H1 self-describes as 'Specification'. No ADR signals: no frontmatter, no status field, no Decision/Consequences sections. No markdown links or explicit file references, so cross_refs is empty. Output filename uses a path-derived suffix instead of a SHA-256 prefix; this classifier has no shell tool available to compute a hash, and the path-derived suffix serves the same collision-avoidance purpose.
